#1674. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#1673. Opinion: Liverpool star has future decided after major transfer update, journalist confirms it

Liverpool have a lot of changes that they need to make to their first-team squad.

That is, despite them spending over £150 million on new players in the summer.

Most of their summer additions have had a positive impact on Liverpool this term with Ronald Araujo almost instantly improving the defensive stability of Andoni Iraola's ranks.

However, they're currently fourth in the Premier League table and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

And, the fact that they've recently been beaten by Fenerbahce in the Champions League is also a major concern.

Thanks to this poor form, many different transfer links have started to emerge with the future of one Liverpool star now being more or less confirmed.

Ryan Gravenberch's time at Liverpool could be over as 'good news' expected about Alexis Mac Allister

This season, Alexis Mac Allister has easily been Liverpool's best central midfielder.

Coming into the 2026-27 campaign, fans were less than convinced by the Argentinian after his roller coaster of a season last time around.

But, to everyone's surprise, he's managed to get back to his best and has even chipped in with a few goals and assists.

These performances have made fans demand that the Argentinian is handed a new deal and now, an update from journalist Ismael Mahmoud has more or less confirmed that's what could be about to happen.

This is obviously good news for the 27-year-old but, for Ryan Gravenberch, it's far from ideal.

"We will hear good news in the next 10 days I guess," Mahmoud wrote in response to a quote from Steven Gerrard who stated that he thinks Mac Allister should be offered a new contract.

Why Ryan Gravenberch's time at Liverpool could now be over

Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai were the two midfielders that Liverpool chose to offer new deals to last season.

The midfield duo were in decent form for Arne Slot's men last term but, this season, things just haven't gone to plan.

Neither of them have met expectations but, of the two, Gravenberch is the one who's been benched the most.

Indeed, Szoboszlai's recent knee sprain has kept him out of the action a bit but, in general, Gravenberch has been the one mostly warming the bench.

The Dutchman is only 24 years old so he has a lot of his career left to go but, right now, he just doesn't fit into Liverpool's plans.

He's already proven that he can't play in a double pivot and, since that is one of the main parts of Iraola's system, it's clear that he doesn't really have much of a future left at Anfield, especially if Mac Allister is being offered a new deal.

New midfielders who can be used as defensive midfielders are definitely needed but, right now, it would be silly for Liverpool to let their best central midfielder go, which is why, right now, the future of Gravenberch looks to be on the line.

#1672. Barcelona transfer news: La Liga champions 'learn asking price' for Ajax star Youri Baas ahead of January market

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 12:59, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 13:01

Ajax have reportedly informed Barcelona that Youri Baas will not be allowed to leave the Dutch club in 2027 for less than €34m (£28.4m).

The 23-year-old has made 108 appearances for Ajax since breaking into their first team, scoring seven goals and registering two assists in the process.

Baas has made 11 Champions League appearances for his Amsterdam club, while he is just two short of a century of Eredivisie appearances, with 27 of those coming for NEC Nijmegen during a loan spell in 2023-24.

The Dutchman's performances this season have allegedly attracted a host of attention, with Real Madrid one of the clubs believed to be keen.

Barcelona are also said to have expressed an interest, as the Catalan outfit look to boost their defensive options in January.

According to De Telegraaf, Ajax would not be prepared to sell Baas unless an offer of at least €34m (£28.4m) arrived, such is his importance.

The defender has already made 17 appearances for his Dutch club during the 2026-27 campaign, scoring twice and registering one assist in the process.

Baas, who has a contract with Ajax until June 2028, is capable of playing both centre-back and left-back, which could make him even more valuable for Barcelona.

Recent injuries for Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde exposed a lack of depth in Barcelona's defence, and they are expected to add in that area at the start of 2027.

“I said it during the transfer window, we always talk about what’s best for the team, how we can improve it. It’s something we’re working on. We’ll see. We have a few weeks left before the transfer window opens,” Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick told reporters at the end of October when asked about a potential defensive addition in January.

"We’ve discussed it with Deco (sporting director), Bojan (football coordinator), and my staff. That’s how we do things. If we can, maybe we will."

Baas has already discussed the possibility of moving to Camp Nou.

“I’ve no idea where they’re coming from, but I have seen something. It’s nice, of course,” Baas told VoetbalPrimeur recently when questioned on the alleged interest from Barcelona.

“I think it’s the biggest club in the world. It’s a huge compliment."

Barcelona have also been linked with Jonathan Tah, but a move for the Bayern Munich centre-back in January is viewed as highly unlikely at this stage of proceedings.

#1670. South Korean star Kim Min-su has no goals and no assists, but it's no problem for Rangers boss Derek McInnes

Published: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026

Kim Min-su’s stat sheet since making the big-money move to Rangers over the summer should be the kind of thing that makes a manager legitimately wonder if both he and the club have been taken for a ride.

Twelve games, zero goals, zero assists. A rank-rotten return, on the face of it. So why does Derek McInnes not seem even remotely concerned by the whole palaver?

Well, simply put, he has a set of eyes. He, like everyone else, can clearly see that the South Korean is the heartbeat of everything that has been good about Rangers in an attacking sense ever since he was thrown into the team – even if the numbers don’t quite back it up.

It was the same story in yesterday’s hard-fought – but deserved – 2-0 win away at St Mirren.

It was hard to keep track of the number of times Min-su drifted in from the left-hand side to pick up possession with no opposition player within five yards. That’s not luck, it’s intelligence.

There is nobody playing in Scotland’s top flight more adept at taking the ball on the turn and driving into space either.

South Korean Kim Min-su contributes to all that is good about Rangers' attacking work

Min-su made life difficult for St Mirren during Rangers' 2-0 victory over the Paisley side

Dan Neil scores Rangers' second in a win that keeps them within four points of leaders Celtic

St Mirren couldn’t get near him for the majority of the first hour. They aren’t the first side to experience such difficulties, and they won’t be the last.

In full flight, he is a joy to watch operating in that pocket between the opposition midfield and defence.

It’s the bit after that where things start to become a little trickier for the talented 20-year-old.

He squandered a couple of opportunities to open his account here. The first came after playing a neat one-two with James Penrice late in the first half, with the ball sitting up perfectly for him ten yards out to smash home.

The choice to take one touch too many allowed Declan John to clear the danger.

So much of his game is based on instinct. Indeed, it’s a big part of what makes him such captivating viewing. But his decision-making in front of goal needs a lot of work.

Perhaps he’s guilty of overthinking things too much.

His manager certainly thinks so, admitting post-match that he felt Min-su was becoming ‘obsessed’ with registering his first goal for the club. In key moments, that shows.

A heavy touch early in the second period after being played in by Badredine Bouanani – unusually quiet here on the right – once again suggested he is feeling the pressure.

But let’s not forget, he’s essentially a kid trying to find his feet in a new country, and in a league which couldn’t be more different in terms of speed and style from what he was used to in Spain.

That he has actually managed to settle in so seamlessly should be applauded. It can’t have been an easy transition but he has quickly endeared himself to the supporters.

It’s why they are every bit as desperate as the player himself to get the monkey off his back.

They needn’t worry. If he keeps doing what he’s doing, the goals will come. Of that there is no doubt.

Some context has to be attached to his failure to notch an assist too. It’s a misleading stat, given that it depends entirely on someone else putting the ball away when it counts.

Min-su created multiple chances for his team-mates in Paisley, the best of which saw Kevin Kelsy put through on goal. It’s hardly his fault that the big man fluffed his lines. The Venezuelan has been in good form but had a stinker here.

At some point, everything will come together for Min-su. And it’s not as if he didn’t have an impact in both of Rangers’ goals against St Mirren.

It may have gone unnoticed amongst everything else, but he absolutely busted a gut to get himself into the box in the build-up to Dan Neil’s deflected strike which sealed the points on 61 minutes. That willingness to put the hard yards in off the ball is every bit as impressive as his ability on it.

And it was his pass to Penrice which led to the full-back being clipped by Samuel Ramos inside the box to give Rangers the opportunity to go ahead from the penalty spot early in the first half.

In truth, they may have been a little fortunate to do so. Put it this way, had referee Nick Walsh not given it, there’s not a chance in hell that VAR would have got involved.

Ryan Naderi stepped up to slot into the bottom corner to take his tally to nine for the season in all competitions.

It says a lot about where Naderi's head is that he had the confidence to do so, especially after blowing a great chance from six yards out only moments before. The German-born Czech international is a changed man, all right.

Speaking of confidence, there is no shortage of it at the other end of the park either. At times, the defensive pairing of Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez look like they’re playing five-a-sides.

It’s usually the latter who throws in the odd lapse of concentration to add some peril to proceedings, but yesterday it was the normally dependable Makhanya’s turn to give his manager a few hairy moments. Thankfully for the South African, St Mirren couldn’t take advantage.

Craig McLeish’s men could have no complaints over the final result but could have made things interesting late on had either Eseosa Sule or Calvin Ramsay finished from close range.

It’s now just one win in nine for the Buddies, who – much like last season – just can’t seem to put the ball in the back of the net consistently. That problem plagued them so much that they ended up in the relegation play-off spot last year.

McLeish has done an excellent job since taking over from Stephen Robinson. A far better one than anyone could have possibly predicted. He has changed the style of this team completely in a very short space of time and so you have to trust he will be able to find a solution to their goalscoring issues too.

Rangers might be 13 points better off but they head into the international break also in search of that perfect balance.

When they’re on it, they’re very good. But they are still not commanding games from start to finish with any sort of regularity.

They won’t necessarily have to be pleasing on the eye to end up with their hands on the Premiership trophy come May. Celtic’s triumph last season proved that.

The Rangers supporters will gladly put up with imperfect displays for the next six months if that’s going to be the end result.

And if the likes of Min-su can hit the goal trail sometime soon, there’s a decent chance that’s exactly how things will play out.

#1669. Chelsea legend makes new "massive" Joao Pedro claim amid one-man team accusations (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 11 Nov 2026 13:35

Chelsea are far too reliant on the injured Joao Pedro and are currently unable to function without the Brazilian in the team, Gus Poyet has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The former Brighton & Hove Albion and Watford striker has been a revelation for Xabi Alonso's side in the current Premier League campaign, amassing eight goal involvements from his first six top-flight games - five of his own and three assists.

However, Pedro is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury, during which time the Blues have lost two and won one of their last three Premier League matches against Sunderland, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Pedro also missed September's West London derby with Brentford due to a knee injury, and Chelsea were hammered 3-0 in his absence, as Danny Welbeck struggled to fill the Brazilian's boots up top.

Alonso has also trialled Pedro Neto as a centre-forward in Chelsea's last two games, but the Portugal international failed to make a major impact against either Man Utd or Sunderland, drawing blanks against both.

Chelsea's drop-off in form during Pedro's absence has fuelled suggestions that the Blues are a one-man team, and Poyet is in agreement, the Uruguayan admitting that he had never witnessed a Chelsea team suffer such a dramatic decline in chance creation with one player missing.

Asked if Chelsea are relying too heavily on Pedro, Poyet told Sports Mole via NetBet betting site: "Yes, without any doubt. The difference is massive. I don't remember a Chelsea team losing one player like Joao Pedro and seeing such a dramatic drop in the quality of their chance creation.

"When Didier Drogba was there, it was spectacular, but if it wasn't Drogba, perhaps Shevchenko could come in and the team would still play in the same way. In my time, it was similar with Gianfranco Zola. The team would still create chances.

"Now, they're missing a massive player, but that shouldn't mean they can't play in a similar way. Chelsea look like they can't. The three players up front are incredible, and they need all three of them to be fit and performing every week."

Interestingly, Pedro does not even rank in the top 100 of Premier League players for chances created this season, having only made seven key passes; Brighton & Hove Albion's Pascal Gross tops that list with 29.

Nevertheless, the statistics back up Poyet's argument; Chelsea's average Expected Goals and shots per game both fall by 18% in Premier League matches without Pedro this season, while their chances created declines from 11.5 per game to 8.75 - a 24% decrease.

While Chelsea did generate three Expected Goals against Man United, that performance is caveated by Lisandro Martinez's sending-off and Cole Palmer's penalty; Alonso's men were arguably on the back foot during an 11v11 first half.

Thus far, Welbeck has failed to demonstrate Pedro's ability to drop deep and link play, while Neto does not possess the same physicality that his 6ft 1in teammate possesses.

Alonso was not able to guarantee that Pedro would return to face Leeds United on November 21 before the international break, but if the South American is not back in time and the Whites keep all 11 men on the field, Blues fans may head to Stamford Bridge with a sense of apprehension.

Poyet also questioned Alonso's use of another injury-hit Chelsea star, as the Blues lie fifth in the Premier League table with 16 points from their opening 10 games.

Gus Poyet was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of NetBet.

But at the same time, Liverpool's recruitment team are known for being able to spot a gem, so maybe they have confidence Bele can be special.

#1667. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1666. Liechtenstein vs Azerbaijan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 11 Nov 2026 13:43, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 13:48

Looking to secure their first UEFA Nations League victory in more than six years, Liechtenstein welcome Azerbaijan to the Rheinpark Stadion on Friday night.

The hosts are preparing for their penultimate group-stage fixture, while this will be the fourth and final match of the campaign for Aykhan Abbasov's side.

Led by Konrad Funfstuck, Liechtenstein, who are ranked 202nd in the FIFA World Rankings, are searching for just the third victory of his three-and-a-half-year tenure, with the Blau-Rot boss having recorded two wins, five draws and 29 defeats since taking charge in May 2023.

Funfstuck has been aiming to secure his first Nations League victory as manager of the landlocked Central European nation, but has so far been unable to achieve that in the 2026-27 edition of the competition.

Liechtenstein began their campaign with a 2-0 home defeat to Lithuania before playing out a goalless draw away to their upcoming opponents, while they also suffered 2-0 losses to Malta and Gibraltar in friendly fixtures either side of that Nations League stalemate.

Competing in a three-team group in League D, rather than the usual four-team format, Liechtenstein have played one match fewer than Azerbaijan and Lithuania, although even a rare victory on Friday would be unlikely to lift them into the top two before the final round of fixtures.

The Blau-Rot's most recent victory came earlier this year against Tanzania, when a second-half strike from Ferhat Saglam secured a 1-0 success, another win this week would mark their first in the Nations League since beating fellow minnows San Marino 2-0 in September 2020.

As for the visitors, they make the 2,551-mile journey west looking to build on what has been a largely positive year.

Abbasov, who took charge of Azerbaijan after previously managing their Under-21 side, has guided the National Team to an unbeaten start in the Nations League, with his side sitting top of the group after recording two draws and one victory.

A 1-1 draw away to Lithuania was followed by a goalless stalemate against Friday's opponents, before Azerbaijan claimed their first victory in the competition since 2023 with a 1-0 success in Baku last month.

Across eight matches this calendar year, Azerbaijan have lost just once, suffering a 2-0 defeat to Malta, while recording five victories, including an emphatic 6-1 win over Saint Lucia to begin their positive run.

Should Abbasov's side secure a second Nations League victory on Friday, they will finish top of the group with eight points and an unbeaten record, representing a significant improvement on their 2024-25 campaign, when they failed to win any of their six matches and conceded 17 goals.

The two nations meet for the second time in just over a month after opening October with a goalless draw, which was their first encounter in more than 13 years.

Liechtenstein are likely to name a similar starting XI to the one that featured in their defeat to Gibraltar last month.

Vice-captain and goalkeeper Benjamin Buchel will remain between the posts as he prepares to make his 86th international appearance, while Dennis Salanovic could return to the side after not featuring since June.

Set to earn his 66th cap for his country, Azerbaijan captain Emin Mahmudov is also expected to return to the midfield after starting on the bench in his side's most recent fixture.

Italian-born teenager Lorenzo Mezzotero has featured in Serie B this season and could be in contention to make his international debut, although Mahir Emreli is expected to lead the line as he looks to add to the seven goals he has scored for his country.

Buchel; Meier, Hasler, Beck, Hofer; Zund, Sele, Kranz, Goppel; Luque-Notaro, Salanovic

Balayev; Mammadov, Badalov, Dashdamirov; Mutallimov, Khaybulaev, Isayev, Khaybulayev; Bayramov, Emreli, Mammadov

With Azerbaijan enjoying their best run of form for several years, they will be keen to close out the Nations League in positive fashion.

We see the away side coming away with three points and securing another 1-0 win over Liechtenstein.

#1665. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

An exciting right-back has arrived on the scene who is perfect for Liverpool.

It has been a long dilemma for the Reds just how to replace Trent Alexander-Arnold. Back during the start of 2025, there were still hopes the scouser would stay at Anfield.

However, as the months evolved, Alexander-Arnold's abrupt announcement that he was leaving the club for pastures new forced Liverpool's hands.

Amid a scramble, Jeremie Frimpong was purchased and Conor Bradley promoted.

The latter has subsequently struggled with injury problems. Meanwhile, the former just simply doesn't look like a good fit for Liverpool.

It is telling that in the past two seasons Dominik Szoboszlai has spent a considerable amount of time playing the right-back role and now Ronald Araujo is doing the same - even though neither are natural right-backs.

What do Liverpool need in the right-back position?Araujo has been a fantastic addition in the defensive sense for Liverpool. The Uruguayan brings fervent passion that the fans love. He is a no-nonsense defender who makes excellent challenges and will put his body on the line for the shirt. But he also lacks the attacking edge Liverpool need from a full-back. Andoni Iraola at his previous clubs has always used offensive full-backs who can impact the game in the final third and like to make overlapping runs. Equally, they also need to be good defensively and be comfortable at building out from the back. #1663. AFC Wimbledon vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 11 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 14:46

Returning to League One action after competing in the opening round of the FA Cup, AFC Wimbledon welcome Blackpool to Plough Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Dons suffered a 2-1 defeat to League Two outfit Crewe Alexandra last weekend, while the Seasiders survived a scare against Hornchurch, needing a 118th-minute winner to book their place in the second round, where they will face Salisbury.

Playing their first league match since Halloween, Johnnie Jackson and his Wimbledon side will be desperate to end a run of six league games without a victory, and 10 matches without a win across all competitions, when they take on a Blackpool side they have avoided defeat against in each of their previous five meetings.

With that said, the Dons are unlikely to have entered any previous meeting with the Seasiders in worse form than they find themselves in currently, having followed a 1-0 victory over Doncaster Rovers on September 12 with three league draws and six defeats, while also suffering early exits from the EFL Trophy and FA Cup during their difficult spell.

Taking on high-flying Stockport County at the end of October, Wimbledon entered the final stages with a one-goal advantage but conceded late strikes from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis to suffer another damaging defeat, before facing Crewe last weekend as favourites to progress in the FA Cup.

However, their journey in football's oldest competition came to a premature end as they suffered a 2-1 defeat against fourth-tier Crewe, with Charlie McNeill producing a memorable moment by scoring from the halfway line inside the opening 12 minutes.

With no further cup commitments until next season, Jackson and his side can now focus entirely on their League One campaign as they look to rediscover some much-needed form and move further away from the relegation zone.

As for Blackpool, they avoided an FA Cup upset at the weekend when they faced National League outfit Hornchurch, although Ian Evatt's side were forced to take the scenic route before eventually booking their place in the second round after extra time.

The Seasiders went into the break a goal behind but emerged with renewed purpose and soon drew level through a sweetly struck Jordan Brown volley, before Josh Bowler struck deep into extra time to spare their blushes and prevent what would have been a significant cup upset.

That victory means Evatt's side are now unbeaten in three matches, following an EFL Trophy win over Aston Villa Under-21s and a 1-1 draw away to Sheffield Wednesday, who spent the majority of that league encounter with 10 men.

While just one defeat in their last five matches across all competitions represents a notable improvement for the Seasiders, they still head into their 13th League One fixture of the campaign dangerously close to the relegation zone.

Three wins, three draws and six defeats have given Blackpool a slender one-point cushion over 21st-placed Wigan Athletic, although they do have games in hand on several of the sides immediately above them, while a victory this weekend would see them leapfrog Wimbledon, who currently sit 18th on 13 points.

Following the disappointing defeat to Crewe, Jackson could make a number of changes to his starting XI, although Wimbledon emerged from the cup tie without any fresh injury concerns.

Andy Yiadom came off the bench on Saturday and marked his appearance with a goal, potentially earning himself a starting opportunity for this fixture, with Isaac Ogundere among those most at risk of dropping out.

The Dons remain without forward Mathew Stevens, who continues to recover from a hamstring injury that has kept him sidelined since March.

Stevens scored 26 league goals for Wimbledon across the previous two seasons and has since been replaced by Jayden Stockley, who has impressed during his maiden campaign at the club and is expected to lead the line again as he looks to add to the six League One goals he has scored in 13 appearances.

Blackpool also had a substitute make an immediate impact last time out, with Bowler finding the net from the bench to strengthen his case for a return to the starting XI in London.

Fraser Horsfall made his long-awaited return to action at the end of October in the EFL Trophy but suffered another setback and is set to miss a third consecutive match, having last started a game in April.

The Tangerines are also without Irish midfielder CJ Hamilton and 33-year-old defender Michael Ihiekwe, who are recovering from knee ligament and muscle injuries respectively, while George Honeyman and Niall Ennis are also expected to remain in the treatment room, adding to Evatt's growing list of absentees.

In the absence of captain Honeyman, Karoy Anderson is expected to wear the armband in the centre of midfield.

Bursik; Tilley, Yiadom, Johnson, Seddon, Sasu; Smith, Harrison, Hippolyte; Stockley, Cornick

With these two sides separated by just a single point in the League One table, we expect Saturday's meeting to be a closely contested affair, particularly given that both clubs are in need of points to improve their respective positions.

Wimbledon have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks, but Blackpool's own defensive vulnerabilities could give the hosts an opportunity to end their winless run, and we expect the sides to share the spoils after an entertaining 2-2 draw.

#1661. Opinion: Julian Ward could now make dream Michael Edwards transfer happen for Liverpool

Michael Edwards always wanted to break into the Brazilian transfer market, and now Julian Ward can.

The Americas remain a market Liverpool have yet to fully conquer. Since Brexit, changes to the work-permit system have made it considerably easier for South American players to move to the Premier League. The points-based system favours footballers competing in leading CONMEBOL competitions, opening up an opportunity that several clubs have been quick to exploit.

Brighton are arguably the best example. They identified the potential of Moises Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister early, bringing both to England before eventually selling them for substantial profits.

Their recruitment strategy has shown just how lucrative the South American market can be when approached correctly. And just how many exciting young talents can be found on the continent.

Liverpool's attempts to break into the South American marketNottingham Forest have also started making significant moves in that part of the world, while Chelsea continue to invest heavily in South American talent, particularly at youth level. Manchester City another club who have bought exciting gems and sold them on for profit from the continent. Liverpool, by comparison, have been relatively slow to catch on. But that could be about to change. The Reds recognise there is plenty of untapped potential across the Americas and are looking to expand their scouting network over the coming years. They have tried in the past. Michael Edwards was a big advocate of exploring the market. A move for Rodrygo Goes fell through a couple of times with the Brazilian having set his heart on joining Real Madrid. The likes of Joao Gomes, Andre and Rayan were also targeted in the past. It's an area where Liverpool could find their next big talent before the rest of the Premier League catches up.

#1660. GdS: ‘Ahead of the curve’ – Amorim’s positive start compared to predecessors

Ruben Amorim might not have unanimously won everyone over yet, but AC Milan are off to their best Serie A start in four years.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write this morning that Milan under Amorim have started better than under Massimiliano Allegri in 2025-26, Paulo Fonseca in 2024-25 and even Stefano Pioli’s final season in 2023-24.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The best start belongs to the coach who delivered the Scudetto though, with 31 points in the first eleven rounds of the 2021-22 season, which ended with the most recent Italian league title added to the trophy cabinet.

Amorim has also hit the ground running, with an average that, in previous seasons, would have placed him even higher. A year ago, with 24 points at this same stage of the tournament, Milan would have been the league leaders.

The numbers don’t lie: 24 out of a possible 33 points – garnered through seven wins, three draws, and only one Serie A defeat – amount to 2.18 points per match. By comparison, Allegri had reached 22 points, Fonseca 17 and Pioli also had 22 in his final year.

The coach behind the 2021-22 Scudetto also started with great momentum in the previous season (26 points in 2022-23) and in the 2020-21 campaign (27 points).

These figures were double the 13 points from the 2019–20 season, a campaign that began with Marco Giampaolo at the helm, only for him to be replaced mid-season by Pioli. While still seeking to find that same rhythm in Europe, Milan have been surging in the league.

They got off to a blistering start with wins away at Torino and in their San Siro debut against Venezia, followed by a draw at Juventus – a match in which they were pegged back just minutes from the end -and another stalemate away to Lazio.

After falling two goals behind, Milan fought back against the team currently leading the league. Given Lazio’s subsequent form, that result takes on added significance. Next came a victory over Lecce, followed by a lacklustre draw in Reggio Emilia against Sassuolo.

From that point on, the turning point arrived: four wins in the next five matches, including away victories against Udinese and Genoa away from home, as well as the derby. The only stumble during this stretch was against Bologna.

Sensing that the squad was under significant stress, Amorim has granted a week off, with training set to resume next Monday. For those without other commitments such as international duty, this provides a chance to truly switch off.

Many players have headed away, while those who remained are either following strict injury recovery programs or simply taking a break. This pause is longer than usual: the typical break in professional leagues is generally shorter.

This isn’t the only unusual aspect: the return to training ahead of the match against Frosinone the following week will also take place only after the players returning from international duty have been given ample time to rest.

There are precedents for this, though. For instance, the team was given a Tuesday off just two days before their European away match against Bournemouth. They returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they departed for England. The result was a 3-0 loss and a dark night.

There is certainly enough evidence now to speak of new methods introduced by Amorim and his staff. On the pitch, Rúben has brought in new ideas: training sessions are never overly gruelling, and the data from GPS trackers and distance-monitoring tools is never pushed to ‘excessive’ levels.

“We train by playing,” the Portuguese coach has often explained, implying that matches themselves offer the best opportunities to test tactical schemes and movements. This is especially the case when playing every three days, with such little time between games.

While this approach may have initially raised some eyebrows among the players and was even speculated to be a cause for the cluster of injuries the Rossoneri experienced, such concerns were dispelled once the coach provided further clarification.

In the meantime, no one is taking a break fully. Even while away, every player has been assigned specific training programs to follow, ensuring they return in peak condition to keep the good league form going.

#1659. Singapore vs Paraguay - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 11 Nov 2026 15:30

Singapore will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Paraguay to the National Stadium on Friday.

The hosts currently sit 149th in the FIFA World Rankings, while Paraguay are 116 places above them in 33rd.

Singapore's clash with Paraguay will be their first outing since a crushing 6-0 defeat to Malaysia back in October.

That result capped a disappointing FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign, where they finished third in Group A with three points and failed to reach the playoffs.

Head coach Gavin Lee is using this international break to freshen up his squad, handing a first senior call-up to 21-year-old midfielder Woo Chun Wei and also recalling Saifullah Akbar, Joshua Pereira and Darren Teh.

The game against Paraguay will be followed by another friendly against five-time World Champions Brazil just four days later, with Lee viewing the fixtures as valuable preparation for the 2027 Asian Cup.

Describing them as a "significant challenge" for Singapore, Lee urged his players to "embrace the discomfort" and "work towards arriving at the Asian Cup as the best possible version of ourselves".

Paraguay arrive in Singapore after winning both of their post-World Cup friendlies, picking up a 2-0 win over Bolivia and a 1-0 win over Colombia.

Miguel Almiron bagged a brace against Bolivia, taking his international tally to 12 goals, while Hugo Benitez netted the winner against Colombia on his senior international debut.

Head coach Gustavo Alfaro has selected a 27-man squad for Paraguay's tour of Asia, which includes a trip to Japan following the friendly against Singapore.

Alfaro included four uncapped players and a further 11 names with less than 10 international appearances as he continues to assess his options following the World Cup, which saw Paraguay knocked out in the round of 16 by France.

Singapore are missing the likes of Ikhsan Fandi and Nur Adam Abdullah through injury, while Cardiff City defender Perry Ng will not make his international debut as he is expecting the birth of his first child.

Ilhan Fandi is set to lead the line, with support out wide from Song Ui-young and Glenn Kweh.

Paraguay, meanwhile, could hand Benitez a start with veteran striker Antonio Sanabria currently out injured.

Almiron and Ipswich Town star Julio Enciso are expected to start on the wing, with Mathias Villasanti, Matias Galarza and Damian Bobadilla set to feature in midfield.

#1658. Opinion: Andoni Iraola has just been given a major lifeline at Liverpool

Liverpool have disappointed their fans in more ways than one this season.

Most people thought that Andoni Iraola being brought in would help turn things around at Anfield, especially after they finished fifth in the Premier League last term.

Arne Slot's underperformance as the Reds' boss resulted in him being relieved of his duties at the end of the 2025-26 campaign and gave Liverpool the chance to have a fresh start.

However, now that we're a few months into the new season, things just haven't been going to plan.

Iraola's men are fourth in England's top flight and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

This lack of form has led to questions being asked about the Reds' first-team squad with fans now demanding that new players are brought in during the January window.

With some fans even asking the Reds to seal the future of some of their most important players.

'Good news' is expected to emerge about Alexis Mac Allister soon

The futures of several Liverpool players are under question at the moment.

Iraola has a handful of first-team members who's contracts are set to expire in June 2027.

And, while some of them such as Virgil van Dijk and Alisson are extremely important, for others, it's looking like it'll be the end of the line.

The same situation is occurring in June 2028 with Alexis Mac Allister among the many players who's deals are going to end.

Before the 2026 World Cup, fans wanted the Argentinian to be moved on but, since Iraola was brought in, he's been their best central midfielder by a country mile.

In fact, his performances have forced fans to change their tune and demand that he's given a new deal but, every update that has emerged about his future have all come to the same conclusion, there's no chance.

However, this latest update from journalist Ismael Mahmoud (who was replying to a tweet which said Steven Gerrard believes the midfielder should be offered a new deal) could be about to change that.

"We will hear good news in the next 10 days I guess," he shared via X.

Alexis Mac Allister definitely deserves a new deal at Liverpool

As mentioned, Mac Allister's contribution to Liverpool's first-team squad this term has been nothing short of impressive.

He's taken to the role of being in a double pivot perfectly and, compared to others such as Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, his ability to win duels has been impeccable.

Mac Allister has also chipped in with a couple of goals and assists here and there which further proves how important he's been.

Getting rid of the 27-year-old now would be terrible as, not only do they not have a replacement lined up but, they also have no midfielders as good as him among their ranks.

Right now, this update from Mahmoud is probably the best news to emerge from L4 for a good while.

Because, right now, the Reds must do everything they can to get back to their best and start challenging for silverware again.
