The newspaper reported that the Milan City Council had approved a bipartisan measure to halt the current environmental assessment process for the Generali Stadium project and request a new one that encompasses all the interventions the two clubs intend to undertake.

This includes the demolition of the current stadium once the new stadium is operational. The goal is to make the green light for the work conditional on a prior Health Impact Assessment (HIA).

MilanNews have learned that the City Council’s motion is non-binding, meaning Mayor Sala’s administration will not be obligated to follow the council’s request. More importantly, it does not suspend the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

The two clubs remain calm regarding the next phases, especially since the SEA and the VIS are two separate and distinct phases that must both be addressed before work on the new stadium can begin.

The Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a procedure established by Italian and European legislation that evaluates the environmental sustainability of a plan or program prior to its approval.

It differs from the subsequent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), which instead examines the environmental effects of a specific project prior to its potential authorisation and implementation.

The Council has therefore advanced a request that would not currently be foreseen under normal formal procedures. In any case, the two clubs are confident in the material produced, providing even more than necessary by integrating the Environmental Report with all the health-related details currently available.

Milan and Inter have no intention of avoiding any type of assessment. On the contrary, the EIA is scheduled for early 2027, by spring, with completion expected within a few months. Further investigations into the project and its impacts will therefore be undertaken shortly, as per the timetable.

Yesterday afternoon, Mayor Sala issues a statement on the news that broke, once again emphasising that the project will move forward.

“It’s clear that continuing to call the stadium issue into question is a gift to the right. I don’t want us to delude ourselves into thinking we’ve already won. I respect the City Council’s opinion, but the Council will respect the fact that I have no intention of reconsidering,” he said.

“We’ll discuss it in the City Council, but I have no intention of reconsidering the stadium. We’ve been talking about it for three years; everyone should do what they think best. I will continue to be consistent, and I will try to move forward with the stadium project.”

Councillor Martina Riva also gave a comment to MilanNews too: “Small obstacles? They won’t be a problem, we are convinced of the validity of our operation and we will move forward: the city, the teams and the fans who want a fully accessible stadium deserve it.

“I really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectationsaccessibleI really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectations.”

#1563. How academic freedom is changing around the world — by the numbers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

University staff and students call for better funding for French education at a protest in Lyons.Credit: Antoine Boureau/Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty

Academic freedom is deteriorating globally, according to the Scholars at Risk (SAR) network, a human-rights organization based at New York University.

The network’s latest annual report documents 382 attacks on academic freedom by state authorities, affecting scholars, students and academic institutions in 59 countries and territories, between July 2025 and June 2026. That’s fewer incidents, but across more regions, than the previous year (which had seen 395 attacks in 49 countries and territories). The analysis, titled Free to Think 2026, defines an attack as a violent or fatal assault on scholars and students, wrongful prosecution or imprisonment, sacking or expulsion from institutions or restrictions to academic freedom or to travel.

Attacks on higher education are “about controlling the flow of information”, says Robert Quinn, founding executive director of SAR.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; V-Dem Dataset (https://go.nature.com/47UZF3P)

Tensions between universities and governments “represent some of the front lines of the debates and political clashes happening around the world”, says Mushfiq Mobarak, an economist at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut.

Other events counted in the SAR report include government interference with research topics or funding on ideological grounds. “While often justified in neutral terms — such as fiscal discipline, public accountability, or anti-discrimination — these interventions are often used to impose ideological control”, the SAR report explains.

But academic freedom has substantially improved in some places, notably Bangladesh (see ‘Freedom in figures’). Nature highlights five countries where scholars have experienced recent changes to their freedoms.

Data from the Academic Freedom Index Update 2026 report, published in March, show a steep decline in academic freedom in the United States (see ‘Rapid deterioration’). The trend is very troubling, says Quinn, who notes that it is not limited to the past five years. Its start precedes the return of US President Donald Trump to office in 2025. “The pressures on higher education are not limited to one election [or] one administration,” he says.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; Academic Freedom Index Update 2026

The country’s recent restrictions on immigration, such as travel bans and greater scrutiny of social-media accounts, contributed to a 35% drop in the number of international student visas granted by the United States during the summer of 2025 compared with that of 2024, according to Inside Higher Ed’s analysis of data released by the US State Department.

The government of Indonesia, led by President Prabowo Subianto since 2024, launched a violent crackdown on protests in 2025, which included raids on student demonstrations and suspending students thought to have anti-government views. The same year, the country’s military law was amended to allow officers to take roles in civic institutions without having to resign from the armed forces. Since then, researchers have reported an increased presence of military personnel on campuses and more government surveillance of universities.

Herlambang Wiratraman, who studies law and social justice at Gadjah Mada University in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, helped to establish a legal framework to protect academic freedom. He says that the situation in the country’s universities is getting worse amid intrusions by the current administration, including appointing presidents of universities and controlling research funds and agendas.

In contrast to the overall trend, in Hungary, a government elected in April led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar has rolled back various restrictions on university autonomy that were introduced during Viktor Orbán’s 16-year premiership.

During that time, many universities were managed by trusts run by boards whose members were often political appointees. In 2022, the Council of the European Union froze funds for 21 Hungarian universities and restricted access to the EU’s flagship research programme, Horizon Europe, and its exchange scheme Erasmus+. In October, the EU Council announced that it would restore full participation to these initiatives and release €4.2 billion (US$4.7 billion) in funding for Hungarian universities.

The SAR report says that the new administration in Hungary offers reason for cautious optimism.

“A lot of researchers and scientists are now joining the government,” says Balázs Lengyel, an economic geographer at the Centre for Economic and Regional Studies in Budapest. Many of them are being appointed “at the state-secretary level”.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02998-0

#1562. Montserrat vs Nicaragua - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:59

With a place in the preliminary round of the 2027 Gold Cup at stake, Montserrat will host Nicaragua for the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in showdown at Estadio Cibao, kicking off at midnight UK time on Friday.

The Emerald Boys are in excellent form after four wins on the bounce, while the Blue and White have struggled so far in this competition, suffering four defeats.

Gabriel Calderon's Montserrat are the underdogs on paper, owing to the fact they are the entrants into this play-in from League C, but they have put together an impressive campaign so far.

The Emerald Boys won all four of their clashes in League C's Group A, topping the table with 12 points after four games and qualifying for this stage as the highest-ranked nation in their league.

Calderon's side kicked off with a 2-0 victory over Turks and Caicos Islands, and after successive 3-0 and 2-0 triumphs against the British Virgin Islands, hammered Turks and Caicos 4-1 on home turf.

That flawless streak of wins saw Montserrat score 11 times and concede just once, a defensive record that could be crucial on Friday.

However, it remains to be seen whether the 172nd-ranked nation can maintain that level of solidity up against an opponent 35 places better in FIFA's ratings.

Meanwhile, Juan Cruz Real's Nicaragua have endured a dire Nations League term, failing to avoid defeat even once to date.

The Blue and White finished at the bottom of League A's Group A with zero points to their name, and arrive for this first leg having last earned a victory back in November 2025, when they beat Honduras 2-0 in a World Cup qualifier.

Real's men were downed 3-2 by the Dominican Republic on matchday one of the group stage, falling two goals behind within the first 15 minutes, before fighting back to 2-2 only to see Porto's Pablo Rosario snatch the points with a 97th-minute dagger.

That demoralising loss set the tone for Nicaragua, who followed up with a 6-1 battering by Curacao, a 3-0 thrashing by Costa Rica, and another defeat to the Dominican Republic last time out - 2-1 on October 5.

Looking ahead to Friday's showdown, fans of the visitors will be most concerned by the fact their team conceded 14 goals across just four group matches while netting just four of their own.

With that defensive frailty in mind, manager Real will be desperate to avoid accruing a first-leg deficit that may put the tie beyond Nicaragua before they can dig in for the second leg on home turf.

Hoping to keep up their impressive defensive record, Montserrat look set to start Trent Carter-Rogers in goal, shielded by a centre-back partnership of Nico Gordon and Reading's Jeriel Dorsett.

At the opposite end of the pitch, captain Lyle Taylor should be ready to lead the line, joined in a strike partnership by Ashley Boatswain of Gateshead, while being supported from out wide by Brandon Barzey and the versatile Lenni Cirino.

As for Nicaragua, a five-man backline featuring Justing Cano, Marvin Fletes and Juan Luis Perez at its core is likely to operate in front of San Carlos shot-stopper Jason Vega Carmona.

Joab Gutierrez and Emmanuel Gomez are expected to start as the visitors' wingbacks, aiming to provide width for the attack as well as cover for what has been a vulnerable defence so far in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, Jaime Moreno Ciorciari of Finnish side KuPS will line up as a lone striker, aided by Efrain Mejia and Raheem Cole.

Carter-Rodgers; Kirnon, Gordon, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Comley, Dyer, Cirino; Taylor, Boatswain

Vega Carmona; Gutierrez, Cano, Fletes, Perez, Gomez; R Cole, Moncada, K Cole, Mejia; Moreno Ciorciari

Montserrat proved more than capable of dominating opponents during the group stage, and will be confident of continuing that trend this week.

By contrast, Nicaragua will be low on confidence after suffering a number of damaging defeats to this point, and keeping the scoreline down may be their aim for the first leg.

#1560. Egypt vs Malawi - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 11 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 00:09

Egypt begin a new chapter under Ali Maher when they welcome Malawi to Cairo on Friday for round three of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with the newly appointed head coach having little time to settle in before his first assignment with the national team.

The Pharaohs lead Group B on goal difference after collecting four points from their opening two qualifiers, sitting one point above third-placed visitors.

Maher takes charge of Egypt for the first time following the dismissal of Hossam Hassan on November 7, bringing an abrupt end to his two-year-and-nine-month spell in charge, during which he guided the team to a fourth-placed finish at the 2025 AFCON and qualification for the 2026 World Cup, where they reached the last 16.

Since their defeat to Argentina at the global tournament, the Pharaohs have played three matches, producing a mixture of attacking quality and inconsistency, with the North African side beating South Sudan 5-0 in Juba after opening their qualifying campaign with a goalless draw against Angola.

Hassan's final match in charge was a 1-0 friendly defeat to South Africa in Cairo on October 4, while the Egyptian Football Association cited concerns about the national team's image and stability when announcing the decision to relieve the 60-year-old of his duties.

Although the former coach won 23 of his 39 matches in charge of the Pharaohs (D10, L6), Maher inherits a side that have managed just two victories inside regulation time in their last nine outings, leaving him with the task of bringing greater consistency to the team.

Egypt have also struggled to convince on home soil in recent matches, failing to score in their last two outings in the country, although their record against Friday's opponents offers some encouragement, having won four of their previous six meetings (D1, L1).

Malawi have their own problems to address on the road, having failed to win any of their last five away fixtures, losing three of those matches inside regulation time and failing to score in three.

That poor run reflects the visitors' wider struggles, with Kalisto Pasuwa's side managing just two victories in their last nine outings across all venues (D2, L5), one of which came in the opening round of the AFCON qualifiers when they beat South Sudan 2-1 in Lilongwe.

However, the Flames failed to build on that promising start as they suffered a 3-1 defeat to Angola in their previous qualifier, leaving them under pressure to take something from this encounter, particularly as another loss coupled with an Angola victory would leave them four points behind the qualification places.

The stakes are heightened by Malawi's limited history at the continental tournament, having qualified just three times previously, with their most recent appearance coming in the 2021 edition, when they reached the last 16 for the first time, while Pasuwa has also admitted that securing AFCON qualification will determine his future.

Malawi Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Egypt head coach Maher has recalled Mohamed El Shenawy, Mahmoud Hamdy El Wensh, Mohamed Shehata, Mahmoud Marei and Nasser Maher, while Mahmoud Mamdouh has earned his first senior call-up after making an impressive start to the domestic season.

Captain Mohamed Salah is also available again after missing the previous two outings against South Sudan and South Africa, while Trezeguet has returned from injury and Omar Marmoush is expected to feature in the lineup.

Meanwhile, Mostafa Ziko is suspended after receiving a five-match FIFA ban for his post-match comments at the World Cup, while Hamdy Fathy misses out through injury.

Malawi will be without defender Dennis Chembezi through injury, while forward Mayele Malango is unavailable because of his club's involvement in the USL playoffs and goalkeeper William Thole has been left out due to a lack of playing time at Simba.

Lanjesi Nkhoma has returned after missing the previous three call-ups, while Chikumbutso Salima is also back in the squad after recovering from injury.

#1559. Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson is doomed... a haunted man whose players have given up the ghost

Published: 16:16 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:42 EST, 8 November 2026

Stephen Robinson has looked like a beaten man for weeks. The Aberdeen manager insists he is still up for the fight but the body language suggests otherwise: tired, haunted and so out of explanations for his team’s wretched form that he doesn’t even try to come up with any more.

It is inconceivable that he will continue in the post after another traumatic defeat at Pittodrie yesterday. Not only did Aberdeen lose to Hibs, they gave up the ghost when a second goal went in with 11 minutes left and eventually succumbed to a 4-0 drubbing by the team who had started the day bottom of the league.

Whatever he might say to the contrary, Robinson would probably be just as minded to chuck it, were it not for the compensation that will come his way when he is sacked in the days ahead. And sacked he surely will be, especially now that the international window gives the club some breathing space.

Watching the usually chirpy Robinson have the stuffing knocked out of him by this bruising experience has not been fun. With every passing week, he has looked increasingly worn down by the weight of the club, the wrath of supporters (who never wanted him there in the first place) and the half-hearted efforts of his own players.

Quite apart from their three league wins from 12 and the home defeats by St Johnstone and Falkirk, there has been no sign of a playing style that showed potential. Nobody expected sophisticated football from the Northern Irishman, but even the aggression, physicality and direct approach for which he was renowned elsewhere has been conspicuous by its absence.

Robinson’s Aberdeen seem to be better out of possession, as they showed against Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final, than they are in it. After conceding an early goal to St Johnstone last month, they were given the ball for the next 76 minutes but had no idea what to do with it.

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson shows his despair during the 4-0 defeat by HIbs at Pittodrie

It seems almost inconceivable that Robinson will stay in his post after another traumatic loss

Hibs striker Thibault Klidje rounds off the scoring as Aberdeen collapse in the closing stages

You might get away with that at St Mirren and Motherwell, where he had so much success in previous years, but it’s no use at a club of Aberdeen’s stature. By appointing a manager who was the polar opposite of his predecessor, Jimmy Thelin, the board at Pittodrie had hoped to go back to basics, but now even the fundamentals have gone.

Owner Dave Cormack has tried everything since becoming Aberdeen’s chairman in 2019. Stephen Glass and Barry Robson were young project managers. Thelin was the foreigner with a philosophy. Jim Goodwin and Robinson were the guys with a track record in the Premiership.

All failed, even Thelin, whose historic Scottish Cup triumph had promised so much. At times like these, Alex Ferguson’s miraculous achievements of the 1980s are blamed for casting a long shadow over Pittodrie, but a successful past is no excuse for a failed future.

After all, Derek McInnes was not so weighed down by history that he couldn’t guide Aberdeen to four second-place finishes. Before that, Jimmy Calderwood led them into the last 32 of the UEFA Cup. Goodwin is now faring rather well with Dundee United. And whatever is said about Robinson, he deserved a shot at one of the big jobs.

At what point is it acknowledged that the problem is not so much the managers as the mistakes made by those who appoint them? Aberdeen are lucky to have a benefactor like Cormack who has invested millions in the team and its infrastructure, but the money hasn’t bought them a vision that could be turned into reality.

In 2024, Aberdeen appointed a German consultancy firm to conduct a holistic, top-to-bottom review of their football operations. They appointed Thelin and drew up a three-year plan that would modernise the club and lead it to a sustainable long-term future. One of those who assisted in that process, Lutz Pfannenstiel, later became the club’s sporting director.

Whatever happened to all that? When Thelin ran out of road, Aberdeen’s chief executive, Alan Burrows, turned to Robinson, with whom he had worked at Motherwell. It never felt like he would fit into a framework that had been built around his predecessor, a Swede whose management style could hardly have been more different.

Among the many complaints from disgruntled Aberdeen fans are questions about recruitment. More particularly, who is signing which players? Let’s just say they have their doubts that Pfannenstiel scoured the whole of Europe last summer and came up with Brad Lyons and Toyosi Olusanya.

This is a club that has lost its way, an institution that appears to have given up on joining the dots between its various departments. The crumb of comfort for disillusioned fans is that a new chief executive is just in the door and will surely see this as an opportunity to address the malaise. The role vacated by Burrows in September is now filled by former FA communications executive Adrian Bevington.

Assuming Robinson is asked to clear his desk this week, the challenge for Bevington will not just be to replace him. It won’t just be a matter of getting together with his decision-making colleagues and weighing up a data-based appointment from the Netherlands. Or using his negotiating skills to lure John McGlynn from Falkirk.

It will be about the club as a whole. About ensuring that everyone at Aberdeen is singing from the same hymn sheet, with shared goals, a common vision and a manager who fits into the grand plan. It won’t guarantee them success, but it will bring about progress. And right now, that is as much as Aberdeen can ask.

#1558. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1557. GdS: Milan open to Camarda loan to aid development – move abroad also possible

AC Milan’s plan to strengthen the attack in January could have a knock-on impact on Francesco Camarda’s fate, a report claims.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport makes the bold claim that Milan are readying a winter attempt for Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge. His price tag is already €50m, but the idea is to invest in the young striker and potentially pair him with Goncalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tresoldi’s fate intersects with that of Camarda. The Milan academy graduate has barely exceeded 100 minutes of playing time this season, 119 to be precise: 83 in the Europa League, with a single start against Salzburg, and another 36 in Serie A.

He hasn’t scored and had only one real chance to score, against Bologna. He needs to play to showcase his qualities, so the club believe it’s best to try do this elsewhere, before returning fit and ready to play for the Rossoneri.

The new development is that Camarda could develop at another Serie A team, or potentially return further enriched by experience abroad. There’s no shortage of options outside of Italy, but it will be a dry loan with no option to make it permanent.

Having arrived as a child in the Milan youth academy, he won an U15 Scudetto. He also achieved a historic record: with a federal exemption required because he was still a teenager, Camarda made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on 25 November 2023, late in the match against Fiorentina.

On that occasion, he became the youngest debutant in Serie A history (15 years, 8 months, and 15 days) and the youngest debutant in Milan’s history, surpassing the previous record set by Paolo Maldini, who made his debut at 16 years, 6 months, and 25 days.

In 2024, he signed his first professional contract and began his experience with Milan Futuro, the club’s second team, created specifically to nurture Milan’s talents, without necessarily having the need to send them elsewhere to develop.

That same season, at 16 years and 226 days, he became the youngest Italian player ever to make his Champions League debut. In 2025-26, it was time to try Serie A, where he could consistently play: he moved to Lecce, where, in 23 appearances, he scored his first (and so far only) league goal.

He was bought by the Giallorossi, and then bought back by Milan (who reserved a buy-back clause), with a contract extended until the summer of 2031 in the summer, plus an option for another year.

After progressing through Italy’s youth teams, Camarda truly found his calling with the U21s, scoring four goals in six games. He was also called up to the senior national team, playing for Baldini’s ‘experimental’ squad, making two appearances.

#1556. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1555. Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 17:01 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

#1554. Milan board member reveals players ‘love’ Amorim and Cardinale has ‘great energy’

AC Milan board member Riccardo Stefanelli has revealed the positive impressions he has received from Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim.

Milan have had a mixed start to the season on the field. They have won seven of their first 11 games in Serie A which is a decent return, and puts them in the top four. However, they have lost three of four in the Europa League, leaving them outside the top 24 spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Off the field, things continue to be very busy. Markus Krösche is all set to become the new Head of Football, which the new stadium project was launched late last month, and a bumper deal with Adidas has apparently been signed off on as well.

Stefanelli – a prominent member of AC Milan’s board of directors – spoke to TMW on the night he received the ‘La Clessidra’ award for his career. He answered questions on a number of different topics, including the owner and the head coach.

“I’m honoured. It’s an award that has acquired a very valid meaning over time, I’m happy about it. It was born from a contact with Gerry Cardinale. We met in July 2022 and began discussing football, fantasising about his ideas for the project.

“I remember that conflicting visions arose on how to do football and business, but today the approach taken is the one Cardinale personally wanted, with enthusiasm, confidence, and consistency. I’ve always been a Milan fan, and I couldn’t help but accept Gerry’s proposal.”

“Gerry has a great energy to do well. Milan must achieve sporting goals first, then there are external projects like the stadium, which are very important.

The new stadium is another crucial thing for the owner…

#1553. AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Anil Ananthaswamy is the author of Why Machines Learn (2024).

Artificial-intelligence tools have found solutions to several mathematics and physics problems that had been unresolved for years. Credit: Barbara Sax/AFP/Getty

Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World Steven Strogatz & Alex Townsend Little, Brown and Company (2026)

When I was studying electrical engineering in India in the 1980s, a professor asked our class: “Why do short- and medium-wave radios produce a crackling sound, or static, when a scooter goes past, regardless of the station you are listening to?” None of us knew the answer.

How AI is reshaping discovery in maths and physics

How AI is reshaping discovery in maths and physics

The professor was using the question to introduce a mathematical operation called a Fourier transform. Each time the spark plug in a scooter engine fires, it produces a short pulse of electromagnetic radiation. The Fourier transform reveals that, mathematically, this signal is a summation of thousands of sine and cosine waves. Whatever frequency our radios are tuned to, the pulse produced by the spark plug contains some energy at that frequency, which we hear as static. It was a proverbial ‘aha’ moment for many of us in the class.

Big Math by mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend contains many such aha moments. But the book is so much more. Strogatz and Townsend use the assuredness of mathematicians and the skill of storytellers to paint a vivid portrait of the variety of ways in which mathematics underpins almost every aspect of people’s lives.

The authors start with an inspiring story about Regina Barzilay, a computer scientist who had breast cancer and, after she finished her treatment in 2014, decided to do something about the lack of tools for spotting the early warning signs of the disease. The technology that she needed to achieve her goal already existed — machine learning — but it was mostly being used to recommend films to people and steer online buying behaviour, and was not reaching many of the people who would benefit from its use in health care. Barzilay collaborated with radiologists and computer scientists to develop a machine-learning model that could predict a person’s risk of developing breast cancer within the next five years from a single mammogram.

The breakthrough proof bringing mathematics closer to a grand unified theor

The breakthrough proof bringing mathematics closer to a grand unified theor

In the book, this story is a set-up for talking about the ubiquitousness of what the authors call ‘big math’ — the mathematics behind technologies that are “shaking the foundations of how we work, how we play, how we learn, how we shop and travel and communicate, even how we heal”.

The authors present the book as more of a conversation than a lecture, but warn that their aim isn’t to make maths “cozy or accessible”. Their disclaimer is welcome and follows in the footsteps of other books published in the past fifteen years that haven’t shied away from getting into the weeds of maths. This includes Strogatz’s own books, The Joy of X (2012) and Infinite Powers (2019), as well as Leonard Susskind’s Theoretical Minimum series on classical and quantum mechanics, and Sean Carroll’s series The Biggest Ideas in the Universe, all of which celebrate the nitty-gritty details of maths to varying degrees.

Saying that, Big Math is light on equations, so the book is more accessible than those mentioned above. But it nevertheless reveals the extent to which maths has permeated people’s lives, for better and for worse.

The seeds of big maths were sown a long time ago. Strogatz and Townsend tell a delightful story about Chinese mathematicians solving accounting problems to estimate the edible rice yield expected from bundles of unprocessed rice still in the husk. The authors neatly pivot to explaining that the problem can be expressed in terms of a system of linear equations (in which variables such as x, y and z do not have exponents, and aren’t multiplied by each other), matrices (rectangular arrays of numbers) and vectors (columns of numbers). This puts us squarely in the middle of the type of maths that is central to artificial intelligence; although the Chinese “reckoners” were solving these equations by moving around sticks of bamboo.

The book is suffused with many such historical anecdotes. We learn, for instance, that nineteenth-century mathematician James Joseph Sylvester thought of the matrix (a term that he coined) as a “mother, a generator, an entity that gave birth to other mathematical objects”. This feels eerily prescient, because the manipulation of massive matrices (with hundreds of billions and even trillions of numbers) is at the heart of generative AI.

How to prevent AI from harming mathematics

How to prevent AI from harming mathematics

They also discuss Leon Festinger’s 1949 idea that repeated matrix–vector multiplications (the kind used to solve the paddy problem) can uncover “hidden structures in social networks”. Over subsequent decades, such matrix methods became key to analysing webs of social relationships to “measure influence, detect clusters, and rank individuals by how connected they were”.

The authors also touch on how the board game of Snakes and Ladders can be used to understand a Markov chain, a mathematical formulation that was key to technology company Google’s early search algorithms. In the game, your next move depends only on your current position and the roll of a die. In maths, a Markov chain is a sequence of random events in which the probability of the next state depends only on the current state and not on any previous one.

Another historical anecdote covered in the book is that of George Dantzig, who, as a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1939, arrived late to a statistics class and saw two equations written on the blackboard. Thinking that they were homework assignments, he wrote them down. He eventually solved them, but apologized to his professor for taking a few days to do so. The equations, however, were open, unsolved problems. (The legendary mathematician’s story made it into the 1997 film Good Will Hunting, in which actor Matt Damon’s character, Will Hunting, solves a problem scrawled on a blackboard while working as a janitor at a university.)

#1552. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

At Juve FC, Luca covers match analysis, squad news, and the longer threads that run through a Juventus season. He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1551. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. #1550. Moreira discusses starring in the derby, wearing Kaka’s number and De Winter declining call-up

Diego Moreira has admitted the last few weeks have been ‘complicated’ for AC Milan, but he was delighted to star in the derby.

Having arrived in the summer window for a fee reported to be just over €50m, Moreira has hit the ground running at his new club. The brace against Lazio was a big introduction, inspiring a comeback, then his three goal contributions made it four derby wins in a row for the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is even talk that the fee paid is beginning to look like a bargain, given that the former Benfica man is capable of playing multiple positions but appears to be decisive no matter what. Now, a key role with the national team will follow.

Moreira gave an interview to RTL Sports from the Belgian national team’s training camp, where he would normally be joined by Alexis Saelemaekers and Koni De Winter. However, the former is injured and the latter turned down the call-up.

How have the past few weeks been for you?

“These were quite complicated weeks, because we played so many games back-to-back. We also had some players injured, so it was a very intense period. But it was up to us to prepare well for the derby.

“We know how important a derby is in Italy. We played the match to our fullest, imposing our pace and our game. I was decisive in that match, but, as I said, it was also thanks to the help of my team-mates. It’s something that will remain forever etched in my memory.”

“It’s an honour to wear his number and to represent such a player. But, as I said, I’m building my career and also trying to establish myself. It’s still an honour to wear that number.”

What do you think of De Winter’s decision to decline a call-up?

“It’s a personal matter, his choice. It’s something between him and the coach. I’m not the one who should discuss it, neither in terms of his life nor his playing time.

“It’s a question you should ask him directly. Van Bommel’s trust is certainly a good thing, but that doesn’t mean I should rest on my laurels.”

#1549. Douglas Luiz finally opens his Juventus account as Spalletti hails display at Lecce

Douglas Luiz has finally scored for Juventus. The Brazilian midfielder found the net in Sunday’s 2-0 win at Lecce, more than two years after his €50m move from Aston Villa, and he also set up the opening goal for Weston McKennie.

It was a night that changed the conversation around a player who has spent much of his time in Turin under scrutiny. Luciano Spalletti was quick to single him out afterwards, and the club’s own numbers show just how rare an evening like this has been for him.

According to the standout stats published by Juventus on Monday, this was the first time Douglas Luiz had both scored and assisted in the same match in Europe’s top five leagues. Before Sunday he had made 261 appearances in those competitions without managing it.

The club also points out that he now has two goal involvements from eight Serie A appearances this season, one goal and one assist. In the 2024/25 campaign he played 19 league games for Juventus and failed to register either.

Both contributions came before the break. His free kick was dinked over the Lecce defence for McKennie to break the offside line and slide in on 29 minutes. Twelve minutes later, Federico Gatti laid the ball off and Douglas Luiz hit it first time from outside the box into the far corner.

Douglas Luiz’s first goal in Bianconero! ⚪⚫ pic.twitter.com/g2vTIhUEnF

JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 25, 2026

The midfielder did not dwell on the personal milestone. In comments shared by the club’s press room after the game, he put the result first.

“The most important thing today was to win. I’m really happy with the result because we’ve worked so hard, and I’m delighted for the team. This victory also gives us the confidence we need,” he said.

He was also honest about the second half, when Lecce pushed Juventus back. “We played well in the first half, but I think we could definitely have done better in the second. We need to improve and perform well for the full 90 minutes.”

Speaking to DAZN, he added that the set piece routine involving Teun Koopmeiners is something the squad practises a lot, and that the players were pleased for their coach after a difficult week, as Tuttosport reported.

Spalletti had already explained after the 3-0 defeat by Lazio that he wanted changes, as covered in our piece on the changes Spalletti identified. Since then Juventus have moved to a three-man midfield, and Douglas Luiz has been one of the beneficiaries.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the coach was full of praise for the Brazilian. “He had a great game today, he fought and ran, he battled on all sides and he helped clean up certain situations when we needed him to,” Spalletti said, in quotes reported by Football Italia.

He came off after 82 minutes, replaced by Sarr, having done the bulk of the work in a side that had only 17 outfield players available. With Manuel Locatelli and Khéphren Thuram among the absentees listed in our latest injury update, Spalletti needs exactly this kind of reliability from his remaining midfielders.

One good night does not settle a debate that has followed Douglas Luiz since his arrival. What it does give him is a platform. If he can keep producing this level of energy and quality in a system that suits him, the midfielder who struggled to make an impact in his first season may yet become an important figure for Spalletti this term.

Sources: Juventus FC, Football Italia, Tuttosport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1548. Allegri banned for Juventus reunion as Napoli lodge appeal

Massimiliano Allegri will not be on the Napoli bench when his side visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Serie A’s sporting judge has suspended the former Juventus coach for two matches following his dismissal against Roma, although Napoli have confirmed they will challenge the decision.

The ban means one of the most talked about reunions of the autumn could take place without its main character in the dugout, unless the appeal goes Napoli’s way before the weekend.

Allegri was sent off late in Saturday’s 3-3 draw with Roma at the Maradona, reacting furiously after Leonardo Balerdi struck a late equaliser for the visitors. As Football Italia reported, he removed his jacket and walked away before returning and having to be held back by his own staff.

The judge’s ruling, published on Monday and detailed by Sky Sport Italia, goes further than the touchline incident. Allegri was punished for an insulting remark aimed at the match officials in the 90th minute, a seriously disrespectful comment directed at them in the dressing room area afterwards, and aggressive behaviour towards an executive of the opposing club. The first two were noted by the fourth official and the referee, the last by staff working for the federal prosecutor.

On top of the suspension, the 59-year-old has been fined €10,000.

The two games Allegri is set to miss are both away from home. Napoli travel to Monza in the midweek round on Wednesday 28 October, before heading to Turin to face Juventus on Sunday 1 November, with both matches kicking off at 20:45 local time.

If the ban stands, his first game back on the bench would be the home fixture against Lazio on Sunday 8 November.

Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) October 26, 2026

Napoli moved quickly. In a short club statement on Monday afternoon, the Partenopei said that, having requested access to the official documents, they would lodge an appeal against the two match suspension handed to their coach.

Sky Sport Italia notes that a successful appeal would open the door for Allegri to take his place on the bench in Turin. Italian reports suggest the case should be heard before the end of the week, so the picture ought to be clear before Sunday.

For Juventus supporters, any meeting with Allegri carries extra weight. He led the club across two spells, the second of which ended in May 2024, and he remains one of the most successful coaches in its history.

Luciano Spalletti’s side head into the week in a better mood after ending a 35 day wait for a league win with the 2-0 victory at Lecce, which lifted them to seventh on 14 points. Douglas Luiz was among the scorers that night, as covered in our report on his first goal for the club.

Whether or not Allegri is in the dugout, Napoli will arrive as a dangerous opponent. You can follow every twist in his relationship with the Bianconeri on our Massimiliano Allegri page.

Sources: Sky Sport Italia, SSC Napoli, Football Italia

His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1547. CM: Monza CEO confirms interest in nine-goal star Varela – Milan among the suitors

Gustavo Varela is attracting a lot of interest after his start to the season with Monza, and AC Milan have been named as a suitor.

As Calciomercato.com report, Varela is one of the revelations of the season so far, given that he is top scorer in Serie A with nine goals in 10 appearances. Many teams are closely following the former Benfica player’s development, but Monza will not let him go without a fight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Mauro Baldissoni – the CEO of Monza – made this clear when he spoke to Sky from the Social Football Summit in Turin, explaining the position of the club.

“It’s too easy to talk about just one player and too easy to take credit. We did well, but above all, he did well: he was called upon to make a leap, to make an effort, and he did it very well,” he said.

“Now he’s calm and serene, but he knows he hasn’t achieved anything yet. The foundations are there for a great career. The goal is to have him with us until the end of the season. We know he’s being followed by clubs with great ambitions, but we want to keep him as long as possible.

“It’s still mid-November and no real discussions have been had with anyone. We know that the boy has received some interest through his agent and we’ve received some as well. But it’s all very premature.”

Interest has been confirmed, but from whom? Over the past few weeks, the Portuguese has been closely monitored by scouts from various clubs and strongly linked with several Italian big clubs.

Juventus are looking for another centre-forward to give to Spalletti. Milan want a quality alternative to Gonçalo Ramos and are in the hunt, even if Nicolo Tresoldi has been linked. Inter president Beppe Marotta denied the possibility of adding a fifth striker to the squad, but they are always lurking.

Napoli are closely monitoring the situation too. Massimiliano Allegri has outlined his needs for a striker in the summer to replace Lorenzo Lucca (who is set to leave again), so they are among the frontrunners.

Last summer, Monza paid just €2m to acquire him from Benfica and sign him to a contract until 2030. In just two months, his price has skyrocketed and the asking price is now around €25-30m. Selling in January remains unlikely, unless a big offer is forthcoming.

However, there is the Benfica factor. The Portuguese giants have two clauses in their favour: they will get a 20% share of the capital gain on the player’s future resale, and they have the ability to match any offers that may come from other teams.

#1546. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa
